key_claims: Al-Qaeda is back in Afghanistan with training camps, returning veteran commanders (Amin ul-Haq, Abu Ikhlas al-Masri) and Haqqani-issued identity documents, despite Biden's denial.

The Taliban-al-Qaeda bond is foundational: bin Laden pledged allegiance only to Mullah Omar and sought his approval for 9/11; Taliban requests to refrain from attacks from Afghanistan are a smokescreen for recognition.
Al-Qaeda deliberately no longer announces leaders; Saif al-Adel in Iran is the presumed de facto emir and affiliates maintain strategic silence on Zawahiri's death.
Al-Qaeda will not acknowledge Zawahiri's death because he was killed in Kabul sheltering with an associate of Sirajuddin Haqqani, which embarrasses the Taliban.
Affiliate emirs sit on the Hittin committee and are in the overall line of succession (Droukdel assessed #3; Abu Ubaidah and the AQIM emir in the top five), proving a unified network.
Africa (Sahel, Somalia, Sudan) is the next epicenter; Harmouch argues Sudan could become 'Afghanistan 2.0' and that the RSF has al-Qaeda ties.
Roggio assesses al-Qaeda as a more dangerous strategic enemy than the Islamic State because of its patience, adaptability and willingness to work with others.
